controls.reason: Property ownership, privilege assignments, and recovery settings are queryable, but deciding which webmaster and analytics properties are relevant requires scope judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every property in the approved search and analytics inventory uses individual identities, least-privilege roles, and configured recovery controls.

controls.reason: Configured monitors for inventoried properties do not prove complete property coverage or that all eight signal classes are actually detected and delivered.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed sites can have enabled monitors while a locale host is omitted or the manual-action query is broken. Configuration passes although required monitoring is absent.

controls.reason: A classification schema and counts do not prove that server events are correctly distinguished among discovery, fetch, rendering, redirect, rate-limit, and failure causes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A rendering-resource failure can be mislabeled fetch while every category has counts and source events. The report passes shape checks but does not distinguish the actual problem.

controls.reason: Grouped reports assume complete intended URL and search-engine inventories, while external indexed counts may be sampled or incomplete.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every listed host and locale can report matching counts while an omitted template is largely deindexed. All groups pass but intended versus actual indexing is not fully monitored.

controls.reason: Search-query and landing-page telemetry is measurable, but intent gaps, misleading snippets, harmful results, and content decay require contextual content judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved query and landing-page inventory has current search, support, and freshness measurements.

controls.reason: Monitor-source coverage is objective, but unnecessary sensitive-data collection and privacy sufficiency require specialist judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Accessibility monitoring ingests automated, manual-audit, user-report, support, and production-telemetry sources with configured minimization controls.

controls.reason: Real-user metrics are queryable, but consent, minimization, sampling, retention, privacy, and representative task-success measurement require specialist and empirical judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Real-user performance and task-success telemetry has documented consent, minimization, sampling, and retention configuration.

controls.reason: Event ledgers can omit changes, and deciding which dashboards are relevant requires contextual judgment not supplied by annotation identity matching.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All recorded incidents can be annotated on one declared dashboard while an unrecorded template migration affects another dashboard. The clause passes but relevant annotations are missing.

controls.reason: Active alert definitions do not prove that queries, thresholds, and notification delivery detect sudden harmful changes for each signal.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every alert can be enabled with a threshold that never fires or a broken destination. Coverage fields pass while sudden accessibility or canonical failures produce no alert.

controls.reason: Synthetic executions are objective, but identifying critical pages and sufficient accessibility-sensitive interactions requires contextual scope selection.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every target in the approved synthetic-check inventory has active checks for its applicable page, metadata, indexing, link, form, authentication, and accessibility assertions.

controls.reason: Retention settings are queryable, but long enough to diagnose slow regressions and migrations has no fixed duration or risk model.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Historical crawl, index, traffic, content, accessibility, and performance evidence has explicit retention periods.

controls.reason: Recognizing an unexplained improvement and investigating whether it reflects spam, exposure, bots, measurement error, or indexing requires human causal judgment.
Choosing a systemic component, template, design, test, policy, or platform improvement from repeated defects requires root-cause and prioritization judgment.
Review timestamps can be linked to declared trigger events, but major guidance changes and material audience or content shifts require contextual or specialist classification.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every qualifying trigger in the approved browser, standards, migration, incident, and audience-change register links to a later checklist review.

controls.reason: Public reachability and indexing tests are objective for declared assets, but discovering and classifying all private, personal, secret-bearing, or embargoed content is unbounded and specialist-dependent.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every asset classified private, embargoed, customer-specific, administrative, personal, or secret-bearing is inaccessible and nonindexable from the public network.

controls.reason: Journey tests are objective, but criticality and the required keyboard and assistive-technology combinations depend on users, risk, and supported scope.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared critical journey has successful results for every combination in its approved keyboard and assistive-technology matrix.

controls.reason: Critical-page and error-state inventories are not complete, and selected route fixtures cannot prove correct status behavior across all authorization and failure paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Listed pages can return 404 in fixtures while an omitted account page returns 200 with Not found for another tenant. Tests pass but a critical page still gives misleading success.

controls.reason: Mapping, redirect, monitor, and recovery-plan evidence is objective, but deciding whether a URL migration is large requires a contextual threshold.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every migration marked large has tested mappings and redirects, active monitoring, and a versioned recovery plan.

controls.reason: Bounded crawl simulation can detect declared traps and page counts, but unbounded space and low-value page classification require search and content judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The production route model passes approved crawl-bound and indexable-page-volume checks.

controls.reason: Canonical, noindex, robots, redirect, locale, and cache signals can be extracted, but whether contradictions are material requires search-impact judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every public URL has a machine-computed consistency result across canonical, noindex, robots, redirect, locale, and cache signals.

controls.reason: Matrix test results are objective, but realistic conditions and which content or controls are primary require accessibility and user-context judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every primary item in the approved journey matrix remains present and operable under each declared script, network, third-party, zoom, reflow, and assistive-technology condition.

controls.reason: A non-automation evidence link does not prove a valid WCAG conformance basis; manual scope and conformance judgment require accessibility expertise.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A claim can link to a one-page manual checklist in addition to an overlay. Record validation passes although the evidence is nowhere near sufficient for WCAG conformance.

controls.reason: Structured fields can be compared with visible content and freshness policies, but truth, support, and material visibility require semantic and editorial judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each structured-data, authorship, rating, price, availability, and provenance field has a current visible-content source reference and freshness result.

controls.reason: Required exception fields are objective, but materiality, user impact, and adequacy of a compensating path require accountable accessibility or search judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every accepted accessibility or search defect marked material records owner, impact, compensating path, monitoring, remediation date, and expiry.

controls.reason: Field retention does not prove valid applicability, complete scope and assumptions, or accountable owners, reviewers, and decision authority.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A package can retain placeholder scope, nominal owners, and an unauthorized reviewer with valid dates. All fields exist while the governance record is not substantively valid.

controls.reason: Exact source-revision identifiers and immutable verification records make revision binding a complete objective property.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every objective verification result is bound to the exact assessed source revision.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A result from another or modified revision cannot pass the equality and integrity checks; missing bindings fail or block.

controls.reason: Evidence classes can be required, but deciding representative coverage for success, failure, boundary, misuse, degradation, and recovery is contextual.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The evidence package contains results for every scenario class in the approved behavior matrix.

controls.reason: Severity, impact, compensating-control adequacy, and accountable ownership require judgment; required fields alone do not prove correct retained risk records.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A critical defect can be labeled low, link an irrelevant monitor, and name an inactive owner while all fields pass. The unresolved risk is misrepresented.

controls.reason: One current postdeployment result does not prove that a continuous control continues to operate throughout relevant time and conditions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A daily control can emit one success after deployment and then stop permanently. Its timestamp passes while ongoing control operation is not evidenced.

controls.reason: The change ledger cannot prove every post-snapshot change was captured, and mapping affected controls requires semantic impact judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every recorded commit can map to reassessed controls while an unlogged production flag change is omitted. The clause passes although affected evidence was not reassessed.

controls.reason: Gate behavior is checkable, but identifying a material uncontrolled risk requires accountable risk and user-impact judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Any risk marked material and uncontrolled blocks approval regardless of checklist completion percentage.

controls.reason: A deployed-verification record does not prove that its protocol verifies the outcome claimed by a tool, supplier, certification, or policy.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A supplier security claim can link to a production health check. The record is current and bound but does not verify the claimed security outcome.

controls.reason: Structured rationale codes can reject listed bases, but detecting those motives in free-form Not Applicable text requires contextual interpretation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: A Not Applicable result is rejected when its only declared reasons are difficulty, expense, unfamiliarity, or external ownership.

controls.reason: Failure-response tests can be recorded, but foreseeability, high impact, and sufficiency of detection, containment, recovery, and communication require risk judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every high-impact failure in the approved risk inventory has current evidence for detection, containment, recovery, and communication.

controls.reason: Known surfaces can be inventoried, but proving discovery of every public, authenticated, document, media, embedded, app, authoring, and search endpoint is unbounded.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved scope manifest contains entries for each named surface category.

controls.reason: The surface inventory may omit routes, and selecting applicable public, searchable, shareable, private, or removed states requires product judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed pages can have visibility labels while an unlisted export is publicly reachable, or a private page is mislabeled public. The schema passes but intended surfaces are not identified.

controls.reason: Exact-one directory identities do not prove accepted accountable ownership for the seven accessibility, content, and discovery domains.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Inactive or nominal users can be assigned and resolve successfully while nobody exercises ownership. Cardinality passes without accountability.

controls.reason: Support-matrix fields are observable, but complete and representative user, disability, technology, locale, crawler, and channel scope requires contextual judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The support record documents declared user groups, disability needs, assistive technologies, browsers, devices, locales, engines, crawlers, and channels.

controls.reason: Surface-specific target records are objective, but selecting applicable standards and jurisdictional conformance levels requires legal and accessibility authority.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every product surface and jurisdiction pair has a versioned accessibility conformance target.

controls.reason: User value, accurate representation, legitimate acquisition, and ranking manipulation are semantic and ethical search-strategy judgments.

Source context User experience, web, and content > Accessibility, SEO, Content Quality, and Digital Discoverability > Scope, ownership, and measurable outcomes (docs/engineering/03-user-experience-web-and-content.md:734). The existing atomic clauses retain the full original promise, use an authority capable of observing it, and require bounded complete evidence rather than a policy-existence shortcut.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The plan defines measurable criteria for task completion, accessibility defects, search coverage, crawl errors, indexing, freshness, and performance.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A partial checker that observes only a convenient field while leaving part of “Define measurable success criteria for task completion, accessibility defects, search coverage, crawl errors, indexing, content freshness, and performance.” broken would not satisfy the existing all-clause aggregation. Missing scope, stale evidence, omitted subjects, or a contradictory authoritative source must block rather than pass.

controls.reason: Requirement labels are checkable, but deciding which requirements are mandatory depends on law, contract, and accountable policy interpretation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every accessibility and discoverability requirement is labeled mandatory or aspirational with a source reference.

controls.reason: Third-party components and content can be inventoried and tested, but identifying all items capable of preventing conformance requires architecture and accessibility judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every third-party item in the approved inventory has accessibility and discoverability impact results.

controls.reason: Contract clauses can be checked, but applicable accessibility and supplier obligations require procurement, legal, and domain judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every applicable supplier contract contains accessibility, remediation, metadata, rendering, availability, and change-notification clauses.

controls.reason: Known properties can be listed, but proving the inventory includes every public, alternate, preview, staging, microsite, and retired host is unbounded.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The property inventory contains entries for each named host and lifecycle category.

controls.reason: Proving that no preview, test, administrative, personalized, confidential, or prerelease content is publicly discoverable requires complete content discovery and classification.
Six documentation sections do not prove accurate effects on accessibility and search for every personalized state and experiment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Each section can say no effect while geolocation hides content from crawlers and consent changes keyboard order. Presence passes but behavior is undocumented truthfully.

controls.reason: Linked criteria can be irrelevant, and deciding applicability and adequate accessibility or discoverability acceptance criteria requires semantic review.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every requirement can link to a generic alt text exists check while a dynamic search feature lacks indexability criteria. Links pass but acceptance coverage is missing.

controls.reason: A reporting route can be discovered and tested, but whether it is clear for users requires usability and accessibility evaluation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: A public route accepts accessibility, content, metadata, and search-discovery reports and returns a successful confirmation.

controls.reason: Redesign and platform events can be matched to reviews, but qualifying domain changes, acquisitions, localization expansion, and generated-content impact require scope judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every qualifying trigger in the approved product-change register links to a later scope review.

controls.reason: The configured baseline version is observable, but determining whether a binding requirement mandates another or stricter target requires legal and procurement authority.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each general web surface uses WCAG 2.2 unless its applicability record names a binding alternative or stricter target.

controls.reason: Conformance level and requirement records are observable, but discovering all obligations arising from law, procurement, contract, safety, and research requires specialist judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The accessibility plan records selected conformance level and additional requirements with source references.

controls.reason: Naming a methodology and populating scope and sample fields does not prove representative sampling or correct methodology application.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A plan can call one homepage representative of a thousand templates and pass every field. The evaluation methodology is named but not validly applied.

controls.reason: Process and journey identifiers can be sampled, but completeness and the boundary between a complete process and isolated page require user-task judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every complete process in the approved journey inventory is included as a multi-step evaluation target.

controls.reason: Sample-category coverage is checkable, but representative selection and complete relevant states or variants require accessibility judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The evaluation sample includes entries for each applicable page, template, component, state, error, authenticated, document, media, and dynamic-variant category.

controls.reason: A supported setting matrix and assertions cannot exhaust content states, and readability or loss of function requires accessibility and user judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Fixtures can pass at one viewport while a localized modal becomes unreadable at 400 percent zoom. All approved cases pass but supported content still fails.

controls.reason: Evidence labels for five modalities do not establish expert quality, representative users, adequate scope, or a valid conformance conclusion.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A trivial automated scan plus one-minute manual and user records can satisfy modality presence while critical keyboard journeys remain untested.

controls.reason: Source context User experience, web, and content > Accessibility, SEO, Content Quality, and Digital Discoverability > Accessibility standards and evaluation methodology (docs/engineering/03-user-experience-web-and-content.md:754). The existing atomic clauses retain the full original promise, use an authority capable of observing it, and require bounded complete evidence rather than a policy-existence shortcut.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every evaluation records standards, techniques, tools and versions, assistive technologies, browsers, operating systems, devices, samples, and limitations.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A partial checker that observes only a convenient field while leaving part of “Record the exact standards, techniques, test tools, versions, assistive technologies, browsers, operating systems, devices, samples, and limitations used.” broken would not satisfy the existing all-clause aggregation. Missing scope, stale evidence, omitted subjects, or a contradictory authoritative source must block rather than pass.

controls.reason: Source context User experience, web, and content > Accessibility, SEO, Content Quality, and Digital Discoverability > Accessibility standards and evaluation methodology (docs/engineering/03-user-experience-web-and-content.md:755). The existing atomic clauses retain the full original promise, use an authority capable of observing it, and require bounded complete evidence rather than a policy-existence shortcut.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every evaluation item is labeled normative requirement, informative technique, or tool heuristic with its source reference.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A partial checker that observes only a convenient field while leaving part of “Distinguish normative requirements from informative techniques and tool heuristics.” broken would not satisfy the existing all-clause aggregation. Missing scope, stale evidence, omitted subjects, or a contradictory authoritative source must block rather than pass.

controls.reason: User impact, task blockage, reach, reversibility, and legal or safety significance require accessibility, legal, and risk judgment.

Source context User experience, web, and content > Accessibility, SEO, Content Quality, and Digital Discoverability > Accessibility standards and evaluation methodology (docs/engineering/03-user-experience-web-and-content.md:757). The existing atomic clauses retain the full original promise, use an authority capable of observing it, and require bounded complete evidence rather than a policy-existence shortcut.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Any inaccessible critical journey forces failure regardless of passing low-value page counts.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A partial checker that observes only a convenient field while leaving part of “Do not average inaccessible critical journeys against large numbers of passing low-value pages.” broken would not satisfy the existing all-clause aggregation. Missing scope, stale evidence, omitted subjects, or a contradictory authoritative source must block rather than pass.

controls.reason: Gate records are objective, but criticality, task blockage, and equal effectiveness of an alternative require accessibility and user-impact judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every defect marked task-blocking in a critical journey blocks release unless a verified alternative is recorded.

controls.reason: Independent-review evidence is checkable, but high impact and sector applicability require accessibility, legal, and product-risk classification.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every product marked in an applicable high-impact or named sector has an independent accessibility review.

controls.reason: Relevant disabilities and whether product impact warrants participant inclusion require accountable accessibility and research judgment.
Appropriate compensation and protection of participant privacy and dignity require research-ethics, legal, and contextual judgment.
Statement sections and routes are observable, but accuracy of scope, limitations, and response expectations requires semantic and accountable review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The published accessibility statement contains scope, known limitations, contact routes, and response expectations.

controls.reason: Product-version and date bindings are exact, but material-change classification and sufficient reassessment require accessibility judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every conformance report is bound to a product version and date and is invalidated after a declared material change until reassessed.

controls.reason: Continuously provides no reassessment interval, trigger completeness rule, or evidence-freshness threshold, so a fixed cadence cannot be evaluated.
Whether a native element satisfies required behavior and should replace a custom control requires interaction and accessibility design judgment.
Title presence and duplicate strings are detectable, but meaningfulness and reflection of page purpose require content judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every page has a nonempty title unique within its declared page set.

controls.reason: Heading levels can be parsed, but whether their hierarchy logically communicates document structure rather than styling requires semantic content review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Rendered headings form a syntactically valid level hierarchy and are exposed in the accessibility tree.

controls.reason: DOM and accessibility-tree roles can be inspected, but complete and correct programmatic exposure of semantic relationships depends on content meaning.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared landmark, region, list, table, definition, quotation, and emphasis item has the expected programmatic role.

controls.reason: Accessible names, roles, values, and states are extractable, but accuracy and when descriptions are needed require semantic and accessibility judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every interactive element exposes nonempty name, supported role, current value and state, and any description declared required.

controls.reason: Consistency sufficient for speech-input identification is a user interaction outcome without a defined command grammar, population, or threshold.
Alternative presence is detectable, but equivalence and informativeness for images, charts, maps, and controls require human semantic judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every nondecorative visual item has a linked text alternative exposed programmatically.

controls.reason: Accessibility-tree suppression is testable, but deciding which content is truly decorative requires semantic context.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every item classified decorative is absent from the accessibility tree or marked decorative by supported semantics.

controls.reason: Alternative artifact presence is objective, but visual complexity and equivalence of a description, table, or transcript require human review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every visual marked complex has a long description, data table, transcript, or equivalent-alternative reference.

controls.reason: Image-of-text detection is possible, but whether real text can provide the same presentation and whether an exception is legitimate require accessibility judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every detected image of text has an explicit exception record or an equivalent real-text implementation.

controls.reason: Table header, caption, scope, and relationship markup is inspectable, but understandability without visual position requires content and user judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every data table exposes captions and header relationships through supported table semantics.

controls.reason: Declared asynchronous-state fixtures do not enumerate every update path or prove messages are useful and timely for assistive technology.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A loading fixture can announce correctly while a background save failure updates silently. All listed states pass but an asynchronous update remains inaccessible.

controls.reason: Accessibility-tree equality to declared snapshots does not prove that semantic order and relationships remain meaningful to users through every transformation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A virtualized table can match a flawed expected snapshot while screen-reader reading order is confusing. Fixtures pass but semantics are not preserved.

controls.reason: Widget keyboard and semantic tests can compare established patterns, but whether a custom widget poorly reproduces a native control is a design judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every custom widget passes its approved role, state, focus, and keyboard interaction contract.

controls.reason: ARIA syntax and supported-role validation are deterministic, but where ARIA is needed and whether it conceals broken semantics require contextual review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: All rendered ARIA roles, states, and properties are supported, valid, and allowed for their host elements.

controls.reason: Markup validation and accessibility-tree comparison are objective, but valid enough and consistent semantics have no fixed completeness or tolerance here.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Generated markup passes the approved parser and produces stable expected accessibility-tree snapshots.

controls.reason: Language attributes are inspectable, but detecting every natural-language change and validating the declared language against content require semantic judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every page has a declared language and every authored language-change span in the content manifest has a matching language attribute.

controls.reason: Document tags and alternatives are inspectable, but correct reading order and semantic relationships require content and accessibility judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every exported document exposes reading-order, relationship, and alternative-content structures to the approved document accessibility inspector.

controls.reason: The approved action inventory can omit controls, and selected keyboard paths do not prove operability across state, role, locale, and error conditions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every listed button can work by keyboard while an unlisted drag handle or error-state control still needs a pointer. The suite passes but not every actionable function is operable.

controls.reason: Finite tab and escape tests cannot prove that no keyboard-only sequence becomes trapped across dynamic focus states and nested interactions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A dialog exits in the fixture but traps focus after a validation error or nested popup. All documented exits pass while another reachable keyboard sequence remains trapped.

controls.reason: Focus order can be enumerated, but whether it logically follows meaning and task sequence requires semantic interaction judgment.
Contrast and area are measurable, but clearly visible and complete focus-state coverage require visual judgment and a complete element-state inventory.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every tested default control can meet thresholds while a focus ring is obscured on a patterned background or missing in an unlisted state. Numeric fixtures pass but focus is not clearly visible.

controls.reason: A viewport matrix cannot exhaust overlay, keyboard, zoom, locale, and dynamic layout combinations that may obscure focused elements.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All standard viewports can pass while a translated banner plus virtual keyboard covers the submit button. The matrix passes but focused content is hidden in a supported combination.

controls.reason: Focus movement is observable, but intentional and correct destinations after each context change require interaction-design judgment.
The returned focus node is observable, but whether its location is sensible after temporary surfaces close depends on the task and user context.
Identifying repeated blocks and whether alternative navigation is equivalent requires page-structure and user-flow judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A page can declare no repeated block or provide a skip link to the wrong landmark. The fixture passes its declared destination while repeated navigation remains burdensome.

controls.reason: Shortcut safety depends on assistive technology, browser, locale, focus, and platform combinations not bounded by a few collision tests.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A shortcut can remap in the tested screen reader but conflict in another supported voice or keyboard layout. All fixtures pass while a single-character conflict remains.

controls.reason: The drag-action inventory may omit interactions, and same declared outcome does not prove functional equivalence across data and state paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A card reorder fixture has buttons while an unlisted map drag has no alternative, or the button loses metadata. Tests pass but drag functionality is not fully accessible.

controls.reason: Complex-gesture inventories and declared outcomes can omit gestures or meaningful side effects, so selected alternatives do not prove universal equivalence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Pinch zoom can have buttons in fixtures while a path gesture is unlisted, or the alternative skips precision state. The suite passes though a complex gesture lacks an equivalent.

controls.reason: Target geometry is measurable, but large enough and sufficient separation depend on the target population, context, and an unstated threshold.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every pointer target has recorded size and separation measurements across supported layouts.

controls.reason: Which actions need cancellation or reversal is a consequence judgment, so testing only actions marked cancellation-required can omit harmful pointer-down behavior.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A destructive selection can be mislabeled cancellation-not-required and commit on pointer-down. Every marked action passes while the original safety rule is violated.

controls.reason: Consequential-action classification and an approved undo path require judgment, while fixtures cannot prove reversal under all side effects.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A charge action can be omitted from the consequential list or its undo reverse UI state but not payment. Tests pass while consequential effects cannot truly be undone.

controls.reason: Motion-input dependencies and alternative paths are testable, but whether an accessible alternative can be provided requires feasibility and accessibility judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared motion, shaking, tilting, or biometric gesture has a tested non-motion alternative or an exception record.

controls.reason: Voice activation varies by engine, locale, pronunciation, hidden accessible names, and control state beyond a finite declared fixture set.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Visible text can activate in one English engine while a supported locale or duplicate label activates the wrong control. Every listed test passes but voice use still fails.

controls.reason: Alternative-input test results are objective, but relevance of switch, voice, eye-gaze, and other modes to the supported population requires user-scope judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every alternative-input mode declared relevant has current critical-journey test evidence.

controls.reason: Test outcomes are observable, but slower input has no defined timing profile and correct timeout or focus behavior requires task-specific expectations.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every scenario in the approved slow-input and assistive-technology matrix has a current timeout, focus, and interaction result.

controls.reason: Numeric contrast is bounded for known pixels, but identifying meaningful visuals and every responsive, interactive, theme, and data state requires specialist judgment and complete inventory.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Default icons can meet thresholds while an unlisted chart series or hover state does not. Tested colors pass but meaningful information still lacks required contrast.

controls.reason: Sensory-channel usage can be detected, but whether information is meaningful and has a sufficient second channel requires semantic accessibility review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every state or message marked meaningful has at least two declared sensory or programmatic cues.

controls.reason: Presence and reachability assertions do not fully decide readability or loss of meaning across text, language, viewport, and user settings.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All declared English content can remain present at 200 percent while localized labels overlap and become unreadable. Fixtures pass but readability is lost.

controls.reason: Two-dimensional scrolling is mechanically detectable, but whether content intrinsically requires it is a contextual content judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every tested reflow viewport avoids two-dimensional scrolling unless the content item has an approved intrinsic-layout exception.

controls.reason: Clipping, overlap, and disappearance are detectable, but unusable overlays require interaction and task judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Supported zoom and viewport snapshots contain no detected clipping, overlap, disappearance, or blocked declared control.

controls.reason: Which preferences are available and what it means to honor each preference require platform and accessibility interpretation across incomplete combinations.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Reduced motion can be honored in one page while an unlisted canvas ignores it, or high contrast response is technically changed but unusable. Declared tests pass without honoring every setting.

controls.reason: No tested sequence exceeds a threshold is weaker than no reachable visual pattern exceeds it; dynamic frames and generated content are not completely inventoried.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Bundled videos can pass frame analysis while an experiment generates a flashing animation at runtime. All tested sequences pass but the product can exceed seizure thresholds.

controls.reason: Control presence and behavior are testable, but determining where pause, stop, hide, or reduction is required depends on timing and accessibility applicability.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every dynamic item marked control-required has a tested pause, stop, hide, or reduce control.

controls.reason: Immediately reachable is not given a time or interaction bound, and autoplay paths can vary by browser and user state.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A stop control can appear after ten seconds and be called immediate, while tests on one browser pass. Users still receive uncontrolled autoplay audio.

controls.reason: Caption-track presence and synchronization do not prove the captions are accurate, complete, and meaningful for prerecorded or live content.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A perfectly synchronized track can contain unrelated words. Timing tests pass while required captions do not communicate the audio.

controls.reason: Transcript and alternative presence is objective, but equivalence for audio-only and video-only meaning requires human content review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every audio-only item has a transcript and every video-only item has a linked alternative artifact.

controls.reason: Description tracks are detectable, but importance of visual information, equivalence, and where description is required need accessibility and editorial judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every visual segment marked description-required has an audio-description or equivalent-description reference.

controls.reason: Keyboard events and accessibility-tree fields are partial; visible and usable media controls require visual and assistive-technology evaluation across states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Controls can have roles and accept Enter while focus is invisible or a screen reader cannot operate the timeline. Assertions pass but controls are not usable.

controls.reason: Caption timing is measurable and cue fields are inspectable, but correct speaker identification, sound cues, and readability require editorial judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every caption track meets its timing tolerance and includes declared speaker and relevant sound-cue fields.

controls.reason: Contrast and toast duration are measurable, but determining which information is essential requires product and content judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every item marked essential has a persistent programmatic presentation meeting its contrast requirement.

controls.reason: Chart labels, units, scales, uncertainty fields, and data links are inspectable, but completeness and accessible explanation of relationships require semantic review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every chart exposes labels, units, scales, declared relationships, uncertainty, and an underlying-data link.

controls.reason: Alternative presence can be checked, but whether map information and tasks are essential and equivalently supported requires user-task judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every map task marked essential has a tested non-map alternative.

controls.reason: Programmatic or pixel visibility assertions do not fully decide perceivability of controls, errors, selection, and state in high-contrast combinations.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All elements can occupy visible pixels while selected and unselected states render identically to a user. Fixtures pass but state is not perceivable.

controls.reason: Suitable line length, typography, hierarchy, density, and cognitive access require reader evaluation, with no audience, task, measure, or threshold defined.
Distracting classification and effective user control require human judgment, so testing only marked media can omit genuinely distracting content.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A rapidly moving carousel can be marked not distracting and have no pause control. Every marked item passes while users cannot control the distraction.

controls.reason: Clear, concrete, consistent, and audience-appropriate language require content and user comprehension evaluation without fixed measures or thresholds.
Unfamiliarity, point of need, and sufficient explanation of terms, icons, and consequences depend on audience knowledge and task context.
Repeated strings and control identities can be compared, but semantic consistency across navigation, help, and labels requires content and interaction judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Repeated controls and labels with the same declared function use consistent programmatic identifiers and displayed terminology.

controls.reason: Whether steps are understandable and progress information is sufficient requires user testing with undefined tasks, populations, and thresholds.
Review, correction, save, and resume capabilities are testable, but complex and high-stakes applicability requires product, legal, and risk judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every task marked complex or high-stakes supports tested review, correction, save, and resume paths.

controls.reason: Minimized memory burden and whether re-entry is avoidable depend on user cognition, data availability, privacy, and task context.
Deceptive urgency, confusing defaults, hidden costs, forced continuity, and dark patterns require ethical, consumer-protection, legal, and user-context judgment.
Label associations and visibility are testable, but whether an unlabeled control has an unambiguous accessible equivalent requires semantic review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every form control has a visible and programmatically associated label unless linked to an approved equivalent-label exception.

controls.reason: Source context User experience, web, and content > Accessibility, SEO, Content Quality, and Digital Discoverability > Cognitive accessibility, forms, authentication, and error prevention (docs/engineering/03-user-experience-web-and-content.md:841). The existing atomic clauses retain the full original promise, use an authority capable of observing it, and require bounded complete evidence rather than a policy-existence shortcut.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Before submission, every field exposes its declared required status, format, constraints, and examples.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A partial checker that observes only a convenient field while leaving part of “Identify required fields, formats, constraints, and examples before submission.” broken would not satisfy the existing all-clause aggregation. Missing scope, stale evidence, omitted subjects, or a contradictory authoritative source must block rather than pass.

controls.reason: Input-purpose and autocomplete tokens are statically inspectable, but where they improve accessibility and privacy requires contextual and privacy judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every field marked autocomplete-applicable uses a supported purpose and autocomplete token.

controls.reason: Source context User experience, web, and content > Accessibility, SEO, Content Quality, and Digital Discoverability > Cognitive accessibility, forms, authentication, and error prevention (docs/engineering/03-user-experience-web-and-content.md:843). The existing atomic clauses retain the full original promise, use an authority capable of observing it, and require bounded complete evidence rather than a policy-existence shortcut.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every field error is programmatically associated with its field, and multi-field failure produces an accessible summary linking to each error.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A partial checker that observes only a convenient field while leaving part of “Associate errors with the affected fields and provide an accessible error summary for multi-field failures.” broken would not satisfy the existing all-clause aggregation. Missing scope, stale evidence, omitted subjects, or a contradictory authoritative source must block rather than pass.

controls.reason: Plain language and specificity of recovery instructions are comprehension outcomes without a defined audience, test protocol, or threshold.
Selected recoverable errors and repeat attempts do not exhaust concurrency, retry, timeout, and side-effect paths needed to prove preservation and duplicate prevention.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A form can preserve input on validation errors and deduplicate sequential clicks while two concurrent retries create duplicate payments. Fixtures pass but duplicate submission remains possible.

controls.reason: Confirmation and reversal paths are testable, but legal, financial, destructive, and high-impact applicability requires risk and legal judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every submission marked consequential supports at least one tested confirmation, review, undo, or reversal mechanism.

controls.reason: Warning and extension behavior are executable, but when preservation is required and sufficient warning time require policy, legal, and user-context judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every session marked expiry-warning-required presents a warning and supports the declared extension or data-preservation path.

controls.reason: A successful alternative in declared journeys does not prove every user can authenticate without the prohibited cognitive task across recovery and risk states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The happy path can use a password manager while suspicious-login recovery requires distorted CAPTCHA transcription. All listed journeys pass but authentication still depends solely on a cognitive task in a reachable state.

controls.reason: Successful fixtures do not establish that multifactor and recovery methods are accessible to users with different disabilities and supported assistive technology.
controls.counterexample_analysis: One password manager and SMS flow can complete while the only recovery option is unusable by screen reader. Scenarios pass but accessible recovery is absent.

controls.reason: Barrier inventories can omit inaccessible states, and determining that an alternative is accessible and equivalent requires specialist and user evidence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A CAPTCHA flow can list an audio alternative that is unintelligible, or a device-loss path is omitted. Execution succeeds in fixtures while no accessible alternative exists for affected users.

controls.reason: Support-route independence is testable, but whether the route itself is accessible and sufficient requires broader user evaluation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every help and human-support route can be reached without completing the barrier that triggered support and passes declared accessibility assertions.

controls.reason: A fixed error suite across four modes cannot exhaust form, account, network, and state errors or assistive-technology combinations.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All declared invalid-field cases can recover while session-expiry recovery loses focus in a supported screen reader. The suite passes but error recovery remains broken.

controls.reason: Cross-matrix tests are objective, but representative critical journeys and supported browser, device, and assistive-technology scope require contextual selection.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared critical journey has current results for every cell in the approved support matrix.

controls.reason: Screen-reader/browser matrix coverage is measurable, but multiple major and appropriate combinations depend on the user population and market.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved test matrix contains at least two declared major screen-reader and browser combinations with current results.

controls.reason: Capability test evidence is objective, but applicability to the supported population requires accessibility and product judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared applicable magnification, zoom, reflow, voice, switch, caption, and platform-setting mode has current results.

controls.reason: Orientation-lock behavior is detectable, but whether a specific orientation is essential requires task and accessibility judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every orientation-locked surface has an approved essential-orientation exception; all others operate in supported orientations.

controls.reason: Supported geometry matrices cannot exhaust keyboard types, cutouts, zoom levels, orientation, language, banners, and dynamic content combinations.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Standard devices can pass while a localized instruction is covered by a floating keyboard on a supported phone. Fixtures pass but controls are obscured.

controls.reason: Accessibility and visual orders can be extracted, but whether they match the intended task order requires semantic interaction judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Mobile accessibility-tree traversal order matches the declared visual-order identifiers for each tested task.

controls.reason: Applying broad WCAG principles and platform guidance to native and hybrid applications requires qualified accessibility interpretation and platform context.
A bound suite can miss offline-specific interaction and content states, and accessibility cannot be reduced to selected automated assertions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Cached pages can pass scans while offline error recovery traps keyboard focus. Every declared mode has a green suite but accessibility is not preserved.

controls.reason: Operability assertions can be tested, but understandability of notifications, deep links, shares, widgets, and dialogs requires user and content judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared system-integration surface passes its supported input and programmatic-name, role, state, and focus assertions.

controls.reason: Document validators provide bounded evidence, but applicable standards and complete accessibility for diverse PDF, office, email, and downloads require specialist judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every downloadable document passes the validator for its selected applicable document standard.

controls.reason: Structural equality cannot prove correct reading order, alternate-text meaning, table interpretation, or link purpose after conversion.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A converted PDF can retain tags and alternate-text fields while the reading order is illogical and alt text wrong. Assertions pass but semantics are not preserved.

controls.reason: OCR and structural fields are inspectable, but accuracy, remediation sufficiency, and when accessible text is required need human and legal accessibility judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every scanned-image document marked accessible-text-required has OCR output and structural-remediation evidence.

controls.reason: Alternative artifact and route behavior are testable, but whether a format fails user needs and an alternative is equivalent require user judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every document marked unable-to-meet-needs has a reachable accessible HTML or equivalent alternative.

controls.reason: Print and export differences are mechanically detectable, but essential information and overall accessibility require semantic review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Print and export outputs preserve every item marked essential and pass their declared accessibility assertions.

controls.reason: The upgrade ledger and regression suite may omit relevant changes, assistive technologies, components, and behavioral states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every recorded browser upgrade can pass the suite while an unrecorded PDF generator update breaks a supported screen reader. Both clauses pass but compatibility regressed.

controls.reason: Unsupported-combination records and alternatives are observable, but whether an alternative is workable requires user and task judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every unsupported combination is documented and links to a tested alternative route.

controls.reason: Product-role declarations and guidance references are checkable, but whether UAAG guidance applies and how to use informative provisions require specialist interpretation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every product declared a user agent has a UAAG 2.0 applicability and guidance-use record.

controls.reason: Perceivability, operability, understandability, and assistive compatibility of the whole user-agent interface require broad empirical evaluation without a fixed protocol.
Declared API values can be internally consistent yet semantically wrong, and user-agent surface inventories may omit reachable content and states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A tree can expose a control as a button with the wrong name and order while matching a flawed declaration. Tests pass but useful accessibility information is not exposed.

controls.reason: Expected snapshots can encode incorrect semantics, and transformation cases cannot exhaust reader, translation, annotation, and export behavior.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A translated export can match a declared tree while headings lose their meaning and reading order. Snapshot equality passes but semantics were flattened.

controls.reason: Presentation controls are testable, but platform-role permission and the complete set of relevant presentation characteristics require product and accessibility judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every presentation characteristic declared platform-permitted has a tested user control.

controls.reason: The interaction matrix cannot exhaust browser platform, extension, permission, download, history, setting, and alternative-input states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Keyboard tests can pass in default chrome while a permission dialog or extension state traps focus. Approved cases pass but browser functions remain inaccessible.

controls.reason: Navigation targets and keyboard behavior are testable, but determining which meaningful structures are present requires semantic content interpretation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every structure type declared present exposes a tested navigation command and destination.

controls.reason: Accessible communication of security and permission messages requires comprehension and interaction evaluation without defined users, tasks, or thresholds.
Extension permissions and data flows are queryable, but excessive privilege and informed user control require security, privacy, and usability judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every accessibility extension declares permissions and data flows and exposes versioned user controls for browsing and content data.

controls.reason: Integrated test evidence is objective, but sufficient host, content, accessibility-tree, focus, keyboard, zoom, and assistive coverage requires contextual scope judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every embedded viewer has current integrated results covering the declared host, content, tree, focus, keyboard, zoom, and assistive-technology matrix.

controls.reason: Fallback existence and route behavior are testable, but critical user needs and whether an alternate application is accessible and adequate require user judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every required format or user agent marked unable to meet critical needs has a tested fallback or alternate application.

controls.reason: Source context User experience, web, and content > Accessibility, SEO, Content Quality, and Digital Discoverability > User agents, embedded viewers, media players, and assistive interoperability (docs/engineering/03-user-experience-web-and-content.md:886). The existing atomic clauses retain the full original promise, use an authority capable of observing it, and require bounded complete evidence rather than a policy-existence shortcut.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every user-agent or assistive-technology regression has a product-defect record regardless of underlying content-change status.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A partial checker that observes only a convenient field while leaving part of “Treat user-agent and assistive-technology compatibility regressions as product defects even when the underlying content has not changed.” broken would not satisfy the existing all-clause aggregation. Missing scope, stale evidence, omitted subjects, or a contradictory authoritative source must block rather than pass.

controls.reason: Authoring capability and an ATAG record are observable, but determining applicability and correct use of ATAG 2.0 requires accessibility interpretation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every product declared capable of creating or editing digital content has an ATAG 2.0 applicability and evaluation record.

controls.reason: Accessibility of the whole authoring interface for authors with disabilities requires broad user and assistive-technology evaluation without a fixed protocol.
Output and transformation tests are objective, but accessible by default and complete preservation of meaningful accessibility information require semantic judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Default generation and every declared editing, import, export, copy, and transformation path pass the approved accessibility-structure checks.

controls.reason: Which accessibility information is required depends on content semantics, so testing only metadata marked required can omit real omissions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An informative image can be misclassified decorative, preventing an alt-text prompt, while all declared missing fields trigger correctly. Fixtures pass but authors are not prompted for required information.

controls.reason: Correctness of author-supplied accessibility data and lower quality of a generated replacement are semantic content judgments.
Template, example, validator, suggestion, and preview presence is objective, but whether each is accessible and useful requires broader evaluation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The authoring tool provides versioned templates, examples, validators, repair suggestions, and preview features with declared accessibility checks.

controls.reason: Discoverability and normal-workflow integration of accessibility checking are author usability outcomes without defined tasks, users, or thresholds.
Requirement and test links do not prove that component contracts contain correct accessibility behavior or that tests verify it.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every component can link a generic accessibility note to a lint test. Graph checks pass while keyboard and semantic requirements are absent.

controls.reason: Documentation fields do not prove complete or correct keyboard behavior, semantics, states, constraints, and limitations for each shared component.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A component can fill every field with standard behavior and omit a known focus limitation. The schema passes but consumers lack required documentation.

controls.reason: Individual token thresholds do not prove all token combinations remain accessible, and reviewed exceptions require accountable human judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Each color token can pass alone while two allowed tokens combine with insufficient contrast, or an unauthorized reviewer signs an exception. Both clauses pass but inaccessible tokens remain possible.

controls.reason: Review records and change diffs are objective, but materiality and reviewer qualification require accessibility governance judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every new component and every component change marked material has a pre-merge accessibility review record.

controls.reason: Whether a behavior change is breaking requires semantic judgment, and declared-change records can omit changes or communication recipients.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An accessibility-name change can be mislabeled nonbreaking and receive no notice while every declared break has email evidence. The clause passes but consumers were not informed.

controls.reason: Adoption timestamps and evaluation records can be checked, but sufficient evaluation of diverse third-party experiences requires contextual accessibility review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared third-party widget or flow has an accessibility evaluation dated before adoption.

controls.reason: Contract clauses are observable, but critical barriers, timely remediation, and adequate alternatives require legal, accessibility, and procurement judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every applicable supplier contract requires remediation deadlines or an accessible alternative for barriers classified critical.

controls.reason: The supplier register can avoid marking inaccessible components, and a linked plan can be a placeholder with no feasible replacement or isolation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An inaccessible date picker can be marked acceptable, or its plan say replace someday. Record checks pass while no real mitigation plan exists.

controls.reason: Conformance artifacts can be versioned and scoped, but whether vendor information is evidence-based rather than marketing and substantively current requires review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every vendor accessibility claim links to a dated scoped conformance artifact and supporting evidence.

controls.reason: Integrated production tests are objective, but proving the deployed experience accessible requires complete user, task, and assistive-technology scope judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every supplier component has current integrated-product accessibility test results bound to the deployed version.

controls.reason: Task-evidence presence and score inputs do not prove that procurement evaluated representative tasks or interpreted accessibility correctly.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A vendor can receive a task score from opening its login page while critical authoring flows are inaccessible. The formula uses task evidence but not actual product accessibility.

controls.reason: Declared repeatable defect classes and artifact inventories can omit detectable rules, components, documents, and critical flows.
controls.counterexample_analysis: CI can run checks for listed templates while an unlisted PDF generator has repeatable heading defects. Coverage passes but automatable defects remain unchecked.

controls.reason: Metadata and false-positive or false-negative fields do not prove automation is only a floor or that error rates and rule coverage are measured completely.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Runs can record zero false negatives without a discovery protocol and be used as conformance proof. All fields pass while automation governance violates the rule.

controls.reason: One current script per named area does not prove scripts cover meaningful journeys, platforms, states, and expected outcomes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The keyboard script can test only Tab on the homepage and the cognitive script can be empty boilerplate. Library coverage passes while manual testing is inadequate.

controls.reason: Test assertions are inspectable, but where they are reliable and applicable depends on component and tool behavior.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every test layer marked accessibility-assertion-reliable contains active accessibility assertions.

controls.reason: Change triggers and review records can be matched, but material structure or dependency changes require accessibility impact judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every qualifying content, interaction, navigation, token, document, or dependency change links to a later accessibility review.

controls.reason: Production monitor coverage is queryable, but where monitoring is feasible and sufficient depends on platform and defect detectability.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every defect class declared production-monitorable has an active monitor for names, structure, contrast, dialogs, skip links, or document generation.

controls.reason: Source context User experience, web, and content > Accessibility, SEO, Content Quality, and Digital Discoverability > Accessibility regression, reporting, and operations (docs/engineering/03-user-experience-web-and-content.md:917). The existing atomic clauses retain the full original promise, use an authority capable of observing it, and require bounded complete evidence rather than a policy-existence shortcut.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The accessibility feedback route accepts a report without a diagnosis field or diagnosis-dependent validation.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A partial checker that observes only a convenient field while leaving part of “Collect accessibility feedback without requiring users to disclose a diagnosis.” broken would not satisfy the existing all-clause aggregation. Missing scope, stale evidence, omitted subjects, or a contradictory authoritative source must block rather than pass.

controls.reason: Actual task impact and affected-user severity require accessibility triage judgment beyond automated issue labels.
Alternative availability is testable, but materiality and whether a temporary path is equivalently accessible require accountable user-impact judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every defect marked material and open has a tested temporary alternative path.

controls.reason: Source context User experience, web, and content > Accessibility, SEO, Content Quality, and Digital Discoverability > Accessibility regression, reporting, and operations (docs/engineering/03-user-experience-web-and-content.md:920). The existing atomic clauses retain the full original promise, use an authority capable of observing it, and require bounded complete evidence rather than a policy-existence shortcut.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every fixed defect has a successful retest using the same input mode or assistive technology recorded on the original report.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A partial checker that observes only a convenient field while leaving part of “Retest fixes with the input mode or assistive technology that exposed the defect.” broken would not satisfy the existing all-clause aggregation. Missing scope, stale evidence, omitted subjects, or a contradictory authoritative source must block rather than pass.

controls.reason: Recognizing recurrence, selecting systemic root causes, and choosing component, process, training, or governance fixes require human analysis.
Backlog fields do not prove accountable ownership, correct impact and affected surfaces, useful workaround, or valid closure evidence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A critical screen-reader defect can be labeled minor, name an inactive owner, and close against an unrelated screenshot. The record passes but the backlog is not truthful.

controls.reason: Incident and review links are objective, but deciding that users lost access to an essential function requires user-impact and accessibility judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every accessibility event marked essential-access-loss has operational incident and post-incident review records.

controls.reason: Monitored supplier changes and a bound suite do not prove complete third-party inventory, change detection, or adequate accessibility regression coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An embedded widget can update outside the monitored version feed, or the suite checks only contrast. Recorded changes pass while a supplier regression reaches users.

controls.reason: Recorded diffs can omit real scope or limitation changes, and a review record does not prove a valid specialist review.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All logged changes can link to signed reviews while a known new limitation is never recorded. The clause passes although statements remain stale.

controls.reason: Measurements can be calculated, but critical tasks and meaningful barrier events require user and accessibility context.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The accessibility metrics include task-success rates and barrier frequency for every task declared critical.

controls.reason: Proving that hard pages, states, users, or technologies were not intentionally or silently excluded from metrics requires complete scope knowledge and intent analysis.
Retention fields are queryable, but sufficient evidence for internal, procurement, customer, and regulatory review depends on obligations and review purpose.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Accessibility evaluation evidence has explicit retention and access settings for each declared review audience.

controls.reason: Legitimate content, usefulness, and ranking manipulation are semantic and ethical search-governance concepts requiring human judgment.
Current official policies and technical results are observable, but which search-engine requirements and guidance are applicable requires search and regional context.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every engine in the approved applicability register has current technical, spam-policy, and webmaster-guidance compliance evidence.

controls.reason: People-first value, low-value pages, doorway schemes, and hidden content are semantic editorial and search-policy judgments.
Configured claim text can be scanned, but promises and their practical meaning across ranking, indexing, traffic, rich results, and AI inclusion require semantic review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Published search-performance claims are flagged when they use an approved prohibited guarantee pattern.

controls.reason: Proving search optimization never reduces accessibility, privacy, security, performance, or accuracy is a broad cross-quality causal claim.
Exact-one identities do not prove accepted accountable ownership for technical SEO, editorial, international, migration, or monitoring duties.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Nominal or inactive accounts can fill every domain and resolve successfully while no one owns the work.

controls.reason: Which engines, regional services, vertical products, and crawlers matter is a product and market judgment that a list cannot validate.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The record can omit a regional engine used by customers and still be structurally complete. It documents a list, but not the services that actually matter.

controls.reason: Five policy sections do not prove lawful licensing, training, archival, and retrieval decisions or usable crawler rules.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Each heading can contain allow as text while contracts prohibit training use. Presence passes but the crawler policy is substantively wrong.

controls.reason: Documentation distinction is bounded, but the confidential-asset inventory and access probes cannot prove no asset relies only on crawler compliance.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every listed secret page can require login while an unlisted private PDF is protected only by robots.txt. Both clauses pass but confidentiality still relies on crawler behavior.

controls.reason: Search-visible fields can be compared with page data, but accuracy and semantic reflection of identity, ratings, and availability require editorial judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each search-visible title, description, snippet, date, price, availability, rating, and identity field links to the page source value and freshness result.

controls.reason: Crawler-user response diffs are measurable, but material misleadingness across experiments, personalization, consent, and geolocation requires semantic judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared variant has crawler and user response snapshots with a computed content difference.

controls.reason: Deception and material difference between crawler and user content are semantic intent and impact judgments, not just byte differences.
Disclosure markers and link attributes are inspectable, but when disclosure is required and editorial controls are appropriate require legal and editorial judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every item marked sponsored, affiliate, user-generated, or automated has its declared disclosure and link attributes.

controls.reason: Evidence links are objective, but factual support and sufficiency for medical, legal, financial, safety, and other high-impact claims require domain specialists.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every claim marked factual or high-impact links to current source evidence and review metadata.

controls.reason: Using diagnostic tools without substituting their score for official guidance or product judgment concerns decision practice and accountable interpretation.
External policy change and review timestamps are observable, but major changes and material search decisions require search-governance judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every policy change marked major links to a later search-practice review and recorded decisions.

controls.reason: An intended-public URL inventory cannot prove completeness, and graph reachability in one crawl does not guarantee stable discovery across variants and dynamic states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed pages can be reachable while an omitted locale page has no link, or a temporary experiment link disappears. The graph passes but not every intended page is stably discoverable.

controls.reason: HTTP success and indexing directives are objective, but whether rendered indexable content is usable requires content and crawler interpretation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every intended indexable page returns its declared success status and exposes retrievable indexable content in the crawler test.

controls.reason: Private-page classifications can omit or misclassify resources, and one unauthenticated probe does not cover alternate hosts, methods, caches, and object URLs.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every listed private page can reject GET while an unlisted export or HEAD/object-store URL remains public. Tests pass but a page that must remain private is exposed.

controls.reason: RFC parsing is deterministic, but the universal confidentiality claim depends on a complete asset and access-path inventory not established by tests.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All robots files can conform and listed confidential pages require auth while an omitted document relies only on Disallow. Both clauses pass but robots.txt substitutes for protection.

controls.reason: Relevant host and protocol inventories are assumed complete, and configured monitors do not prove every live robots file is reachable and consistent.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Listed HTTPS hosts can pass while an HTTP, regional, or legacy host serves a different invalid robots file. Both clauses pass but consistency is incomplete.

controls.reason: Blocked-resource graphs are observable, but determining which scripts, styles, images, and resources are required for crawler understanding needs semantic rendering judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every resource marked crawler-required is retrievable by the approved crawler identity.

controls.reason: Public-but-nonindexable resource and crawler inventories can omit URLs or variants, so passing retrieval tests do not prove universal directive exposure.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every listed URL can return noindex to one crawler while an unlisted parameter variant or locale lacks it. Tests pass but public nonindexable content can be indexed.

controls.reason: Header directives are inspectable, but where non-HTML resources should be nonindexable requires search-policy context.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every non-HTML resource marked nonindexable returns its approved response-header indexing directive.

controls.reason: Declared intent determines the required mechanism and can be wrong or incomplete; the resource inventory can also omit robots-only protections.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A confidential download can be mislabeled crawl-only and use Disallow, or remain outside the inventory. Every declared intent passes while robots.txt still substitutes for authentication.

controls.reason: Proving no staging, preview, search, filter, cart, account, admin, debug, or internal page is accidentally indexed requires complete discovery and intent knowledge.
Proving sensitive query parameters never enter any public index, analytics, log, sitemap, or link requires complete data classification and all-scope flow coverage.
Deleted URL and internal-link inventories cannot prove that every deletion and dynamically generated link is included.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed deletions can return correct status and disappear from crawled links while an omitted locale URL remains 200 and linked from a script. Both clauses pass but deleted content remains.

controls.reason: Which maintenance is short and which routes are affected are not objectively complete, so declared-state probes can omit misleading success pages.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Listed API routes can return 503 while an omitted critical page returns 200 with maintenance text. Tests pass but short maintenance still uses misleading success.

controls.reason: Declared error fixtures cannot enumerate every missing identifier, authorization state, dependency failure, and dynamically rendered error body.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known cases can return 404 while an untested malformed ID returns 200 with an error message. The suite passes but a soft error remains.

controls.reason: Failure-mode probes and index directives are testable, but deciding whether fallback content is unintended or misleading requires semantic review.

deterministic_clauses.statement: DNS, TLS, redirect, timeout, and server-failure scenarios do not expose fallback or error responses marked indexable.

controls.reason: Safe crawl bounds and important-content visibility require traffic, capacity, content-value, and discoverability trade-off judgment.
Route families and a bounded crawl limit cannot prove absence of inputs that trigger larger or cyclic URL expansion beyond the tested frontier.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A calendar passes a 10,000-URL simulation while one date parameter creates infinite future pages after that bound. Both clauses pass but a crawl trap exists.

controls.reason: Crawler identity verification is protocol-driven, but classifying scraper or bot abuse separately from legitimate crawling requires behavioral and threat judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every request granted crawler-specific treatment passes the approved identity-verification procedure.

controls.reason: Private media inventories and public probes cannot prove coverage of every CDN alias, signed-link state, cache, method, and document asset.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed private files can reject unauthenticated GET while an omitted CDN alias exposes the same bytes. Tests pass but private media remains public.

controls.reason: Current public tests for declared controls do not prove that every deployed crawl and indexing control was identified or tested with complete outcomes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All registered directives can have a result while an unlisted canonical rule or locale header is untested. The clause passes but production controls are not fully tested.

controls.reason: Encoding stability and volatile identifiers are analyzable, but human understandability and unnecessary state require content and architecture judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every public URL passes the approved encoding, stability, and volatile-state identifier checks.

controls.reason: Canonical signals are extractable, but determining substantial duplication and the intended canonical page requires editorial and search judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every duplicate cluster in the approved content inventory has one intended canonical URL and consistent declared signals.

controls.reason: Declared canonical and locale intent can be incomplete or wrong, and the URL inventory cannot prove coverage of every rendered and generated representation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed URLs can align while an omitted parameter page points to the wrong locale canonical, or the intended target itself is mistaken. Checks pass but declarations remain misaligned.

controls.reason: Material page difference and motivation to suppress duplicate-content warnings require semantic content and intent judgment.
Redirect status and declared move type are directly comparable, but whether routing is genuinely temporary or permanent requires lifecycle intent judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every declared permanent move uses a permanent redirect and every declared temporary route uses a temporary redirect.

controls.reason: Chains and loops are deterministic graph facts, but relevance of destinations and essential path or query meaning require semantic application judgment.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The redirect graph contains no loops or disallowed chains and preserves every path or query segment declared essential.
